page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The configuration provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is constrained at 7.0 GB of RAM, equating to approximately 0.9 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring persistent disk attachments for storage needs, and includes zero bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reflect the limitations of the older generation architecture and constrained memory footprint. Single-core performance is weak, scoring 914.0 in Geekbench and 1109.79 in stress-ng. Multi-core performance reaches 3557.0 on Geekbench and 5820.12 in stress-ng, placing it in the lower 25 percent of tested machines. Memory performance is similarly limited, recording a PassMark memory score of 1273.01 and uncached read bandwidth of 47.28 GB/sec. Data manipulation metrics show moderate capabilities, with Redis reaching 5.51 million SET operations per second and static web throughput measuring 5.09 GB/sec.

Given the high ratio of vCPUs to RAM, the n1-highcpu-8 provides compute concurrency for workloads with low memory demands. It fits batch processing tasks, Clang build compilations, and basic web routing layers. However, the lack of AVX-512 extensions and low RAM-per-core limits its viability for modern large language models, high-performance computing, or memory-intensive database engines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a dedicated x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz, supported by a 45 MB L3 cache. The machine provides 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 0.9 GB per vCPU, with no bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance testing demonstrates entry-tier compute capabilities, scoring 3557.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 6786.78 in PassMark CPU tests. The instance delivers 47.28 GB/sec in large-block read memory bandwidth and manages 5.51 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware instruction support includes AVX and AES, but lacks newer vector extensions like AVX-512. Due to the high core count relative to RAM, the instance is positioned for CPU-bound tasks with minimal memory requirements, including Clang compilations, lightweight web proxying, and background batch processing.
